description: Five long synthetic software-engineering histories of roughly 128k proxy tokens each, generated with NeMo Data Designer and assembled deterministically by datagen/scripts/convert.py.

calibration._comment: Médias MEDIDAS no piloto de case-01 (2026-11-07, scale 0.05). As contagens de blocos abaixo foram derivadas destas médias para que cada caso atinja o seu char_target com ~15% de sobra; convert.py consome em ordem e para no alvo.

cost_model._comment: Estimativas usadas só pelo --dry-run. Os números reais de tokens vêm do metadata.json do Data Designer.

bounds._comment: A invariante que importa é a pressão de tokens (char_target/4 vs janela), não a contagem de mensagens: um caso com blocos menores tem mais mensagens para o mesmo char_target. A faixa é só um sanidade de 'sessão longa multi-turno', medida em 96-221 nos cinco casos convertidos (o dataset antigo usava 72-128).

cases.domain: debugging a Python FastAPI payments service that intermittently returns HTTP 500 under load
cases.description: Long debugging session over a FastAPI payments service: tracebacks, dependency injection wiring, database connection pooling and a race in the retry path.
cases.task: Find why the payments service intermittently returns HTTP 500 under load and propose the minimal fix.

cases.domain: refactoring a large React and TypeScript dashboard frontend from class components to hooks while preserving behaviour
cases.description: Incremental refactor of a React/TypeScript dashboard: component extraction, hook migration, prop drilling removal, and the render-performance regressions that follow.
cases.task: Migrate the dashboard's legacy class components to hooks without changing observable behaviour.

cases.domain: migrating an Apache Airflow ETL pipeline to a new orchestration platform during an active data-quality incident
cases.description: Migration of an Airflow ETL pipeline while a data-quality incident is open: DAG backfills, schema drift, late-arriving partitions and a broken sensor.
cases.task: Complete the pipeline migration while keeping the nightly data-quality checks green.

cases.domain: investigating a flaky integration test in a continuous-integration pipeline that fails only on the shared runner
cases.description: Hunt for a flaky integration test: timing dependence, shared-runner port collisions, test ordering and a fixture that leaks state between cases.
cases.task: Make the flaky integration test deterministic without disabling it.

cases.domain: performing a major version upgrade of a core dependency across a monorepo with several independently released services
cases.description: Major-version dependency upgrade across a monorepo: breaking API changes, lockfile conflicts, deprecation warnings and the services that pin the old version.
cases.task: Upgrade the core dependency across the monorepo and keep every service building.

user_turn.name: body
user_turn.prompt:
You are the human developer in a long pair-programming session about: {{ domain }}.

In this turn you {{ beat }}.

Write ONLY your message to the coding agent, as plain chat text. Between 200 and 420 characters. Be concrete and specific: name real files, functions, versions, environment variables, stack frames or commands. Never write markdown headings, never explain that you are a user, never add a preamble or a sign-off.

assistant_turn.name: body
assistant_turn.prompt:
You are an autonomous coding agent working on: {{ domain }}.

In this turn you {{ beat }}.

Write ONLY your reasoning-and-reply text, as it would appear in the transcript. Between 600 and 1300 characters. Reason like a careful engineer: refer to specific identifiers, line numbers, versions, flags or file paths. Do not invent a final resolution unless the beat asks for a fix. No markdown headings, no preamble, no sign-off.

tool_output.name: body
tool_output.prompt:
Produce the raw stdout of the `{{ tool_name }}` tool during a session about: {{ domain }}.

Write ONLY the tool output itself, exactly as a terminal or file would show it. Between 2500 and 5500 characters. It must look like genuine machine output for that tool:
- read_file: source code with plausible line structure
- grep: many matching lines with file:line: prefixes
- list_dir: a directory tree
- run_tests: a test runner log with passes, failures and a traceback
- shell: command output, possibly with warnings and non-zero exit text
- git_log: commit entries with hashes, authors, dates and messages
- edit_file: a unified diff

Embed realistic specifics: real-looking paths, identifiers, versions, timestamps, hashes, durations, byte counts. Include at least one detail that a later reader would need to recall exactly. No commentary, no markdown fences, no explanation.

values: a named service, queue or bucket

facts.name: fact
facts.prompt:
Invent ONE discrete, checkable fact that could appear during a software engineering session about: {{ domain }}.

The fact must be about {{ facet }}.

It must have exactly one correct short answer. Requirements:
- `statement`: one sentence stating the fact as it would appear in the transcript.
- `answer`: the shortest exact answer, at most six words, with no surrounding sentence.
- `aliases`: two to four other strings that a correct reply might use instead (different units, abbreviations, casing, or an equivalent path). They must all denote the same thing.
- `question`: one direct question, asked at the END of a long session, whose only correct reply is `answer`. It must not contain the answer, and must not restate the whole fact.

Hard constraints:
- The answer must be specific enough that no other plausible value would also be correct.
- Do not use a bare integer that could appear incidentally in other output; prefer a value with a unit, a name, or a path.
- Do not use a timeout or a number of seconds unless the facet asks for a duration.
- Avoid anything vague, subjective, or answerable with more than a few words.
